svg.text: Multi-Agent SOC Triage Swarm — trust boundaries and controls
Project 09 capstone. LLM + agents + MCP + RAG. Dashed outlines mark trust boundaries.
attacker can influence every field here
each agent is a separate context + prompt
the only place actions are approved
one failing alert cannot kill the batch
max LLM calls · tool calls · turns
MCP client + RAG read — the ONLY agent that touches untrusted text
tools: asset · identity · threat-intel · rule-history · related-alerts
max 4 tool calls per alert; emits one fixed-schema JSON finding
no tools. Reads sanitised findings + structured alert metadata only
groups alerts into candidate incidents, sets severity + confidence
must justify severity from evidence, not from raw alert severity
no tools. Drafts contain -> eradicate -> recover -> follow-up actions
drafts advisory actions for analyst review
may not recommend closure of an injection-flagged incident
used by all three agents and by the orchestrator
every stage re-derives its own conclusion from structured evidence;
low-confidence or injection-flagged findings are labelled downstream,
Load only — the orchestrator parses alerts, it never interprets their content.
Alert fenced in <untrusted> + regex injection pre-scan; matches are flagged, never obeyed.
RAG query built from structured alert fields only — free text cannot steer retrieval.
Client-side tool allowlist + per-run call ceiling before any MCP invocation.
Every tool result re-fenced as untrusted data on the way back into the agent.
Handoff sanitiser: schema allowlist, truncation, and re-scan of the agent's own output.
Correlation must assign every alert to exactly one validated incident.
Code classifies recommendations. The analyst approves or denies gated actions.
Budget / circuit breaker bounds LLM calls, tool calls and turns across every hop.
1. Alert free text is the primary injection surface — it is flagged and surfaced to a human, never silently sanitised away.
2. The past-incident corpus is shared mutable context: write access to it is a persistent attack path across all future runs.
3. Severity and grouping are model judgements with no ground truth — the report is advisory input to an analyst, not a verdict.
4. The demo MCP server is read-only; adding any containment tool must move that tool behind the approval gate first.
5. No per-agent identity yet — handoffs are trusted because they are in-process, not because they are authenticated.
